label: UISP Router
description: UISP Router (UISP-R) - 8x 1G RJ45, all eight 27V passive PoE at 30 W/port, + 1x 1G SFP. 10 W max excluding PoE output; 27V 4.4A adapter.

poe.note: DERIVED CEILING, not a quoted budget - Ubiquiti prints no total PoE row for this box. The two figures it does print give the headroom exactly: the included adapter is "27V DC, 4.4A" = 118.8 W, and "Max. power consumption = 10W (Excluding PoE output)", so at most 118.8 - 10 = 108.8 W can leave the eight PSE ports. Recorded as a derived figure in the same shape as devices/antaira/lmp-1002g-sfp-t.json, which subtracts its no-PD draw from its fully-loaded figure; this is arithmetic on two published numbers, not an estimate. Per-port ceiling is the vendor's own: "Max. Passive PoE wattage per port = 30W/27V DC" - eight of those would be 240 W, so the adapter, not the port count, is what stops a full fill. NOT 802.3af/at: the PoE interface row reads "(8) 27V passive PoE: 2-pair (pins 4, 5+/7, 8-) or 4-pair (pins 1, 2, 4, 5+/3, 6, 7, 8-)" with "Passive PoE voltage range = 27V DC" against a 24-28V DC supported input, so the eight ports feed 24/27V passive gear (airMAX/airFiber) and will not negotiate with a 48V 802.3af/at PD. Read 2026-11-19: https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/uisp-r (HTTP 200, 583,910 B, title "UISP Router - Tech Specs") and https://dl.ui.com/ds/uisp-r_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 2,635,831 B, 2 pp, text layer) - both print every row above. The datasheet key is hyphenated per SKU: dl.ui.com/ds/uisp_router_ds.pdf answers 302, and store.ui.com/us/en/products/uisp-router answers 404, while the commerce backend storefrontProduct(slug:"uisp-r") returns displaySku UISP-R, status Available.

notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti's own pages, read 2026-11-19. Networking interface "(8) GbE RJ45 ports" + "(1) 1G SFP port" (datasheet: "(8) 10/100/1000 MbE RJ45 ports", the 10M rung the row now lists); "Power method: External AC/DC adapter", "Power supply: 27V DC, 4.4A power adapter (included)", "Supported voltage range 24-28V DC", "Max. power consumption 10W (Excluding PoE output)"; "PoE interface (8) 27V passive PoE", "Max. Passive PoE wattage per port 30W/27V DC", "Passive PoE voltage range 27V DC". Management is "Ethernet in-band" plus Bluetooth BLE, so the row keeps cli/http-server and gains nothing new. Sources: https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/uisp-r and https://dl.ui.com/ds/uisp-r_ds.pdf. Before this pass all eight copper ports claimed poeOutClass "PoE" (802.3af) with a true poeOut and no wattage, and the row had no poe block at all - so the budget came from the model name, which has no figure in it: 0. engine/simulator.js opens computePoe() with "if (!dev.poeBudget) continue;", so eight documented PSE ports were skipped without an entry, and a MicroPoP router could not power a single airMAX radio while show power inline said nothing at all.
